name: Island Kiwai
confidence_why: Wurm 1977 and Wurm 1973, the only first-hand descriptions, say Island Kiwai has a complex stress system with rhythm patterns beside a low-load two-tone system but that its stress features are yet to be studied in detail, and Wurm 1951's tentative note of first-syllable stress in short words rests on earlier transcriptions and is itself hedged, so the placement is left undetermined and no source disagrees.

catalog_quote: On the phonological level, Island Kiwai and all Kiwaian languages are quite simple, except for their suprasegmental systems. ... Vowel length is absent in Island Kiwai, though frequent in Wabuda and also encountered in the northern languages. The suprasegmental features manifest themselves in a complex stress system with rhythm patterns, and a two-tone system. The functional load of the latter is very low, and this seems to be the same in all Kiwaian languages in which it is met with (it is apparently absent from Wabuda), except for North-Eastern Kiwai (and Arigibi) where it seems to be quite high. The syllable structure is very simple: no consonant clusters occur, and all syllables are open.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Wurm (own fieldwork) says Island Kiwai has a 'complex stress system with rhythm patterns' plus a two-tone (pitch) contrast of very low functional load; he never states which syllable carries stress. His only stress-marked Island Kiwai forms (1973:250) are 'òròbò 'woman' and 'òbó 'water', both initial-stressed; he adds that 'stress features [are] yet to be studied in detail . the other Kiwaian languages'. Landtman 1917 writes acutes on varying syllables (náo, nettóva, Kíwai, Mawáta, busére). Position of word stress therefore undetermined from accessible sources.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing beyond 'rhythm patterns' (implies alternating/secondary stresses, not described).
new_statements.exceptions: None; tone said to be absent in Wabuda and high-load in NE Kiwai (other languages).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about Island Kiwai (the mission standard dialect of Southern Kiwai) at word level; no phrase-level discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: Wurm's 1977 statement is explicitly about Island Kiwai (Glottolog dialect isla1274, the mission-standard dialect of Southern Kiwai sout2949); his 1973 p.226 wording is family-level (Kiwaian kiwa1251) with Southern Kiwai named in the same paragraph. Ray 1907/1931 describe Island Kiwai (Saguane/Iasa) with notes on the Mawata dialect (= Southern Coast Kiwai sout2950). The 'Kiwai Organised Phonology Data' by Clifton cited on Wikipedia is probably Kope (Northeast Kiwai, nort2930), not this language.
